steps.title: Moon Run needs music!
steps.text: Moon Run has a bump, a star, a jump and a winning tune. But it still has no music! Let's write its song.

steps.title: Songs that go down the screen
steps.text: Real chiptune composers often write in a tracker. The song goes down the screen like a ladder, one row at a time.

art.credit: Game Boy. Photo: Evan-Amos, public domain

wow.text: Musicians still make music on old Game Boys, with a tracker called Little Sound DJ.

steps.dad: In the Song Maker, the Tracker button shows your song this way.

steps.title: Our band of four
steps.text: Our song has four channels, like a real chip: a tune, sparkly chords, a bass, and drums.

wow.text: Koji Kondo wrote the Super Mario Bros. music in 1985 with four channels: two square, one triangle and one noise.

steps.intro: {commander}, make the tune. {copilot}, add drums and press Play. Our beat and chords are already in! Save it when you love it.
Play Moon Run with everything you made!

debrief: What worked? What would you change next time?
